newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD not seeking Europe job-creation schemes.
newsitem.headline: German SPD not seeking Europe job-creation schemes.

text.p: Rudolf Scharping, parliamentary faction leader of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said on Tuesday his party favoured new, Europe-wide jobs policies, but this did not mean jobs-creation programmes.

European governments should orient their policies toward increasing employment as much as possible, but that did not mean there should be sanctions against countries that do not meet jobs goals, he said.

The new Socialist government of France on Monday sowed confusion over plans for European monetary union (EMU) by saying it was not ready to approve the stability pact its predecessors had agreed to last December.

Other European leaders had hoped the pact could be finalised at next week's European Union summit in Amsterdam, but that now appears unlikely, as France seeks to make jobs creation a formal EU priority.

Scharping said he understood the new French government's demands, but he did not believe speculation that the French wanted a system where government debts for jobs programmes would be excluded from consideration under the stability pact.
Scharping said he hoped the stability pact, aimed at ensuring that EMU participants maintain sound finances after the start of EMU, could be passed in June.
The SPD leadership said on Monday they hoped EMU would start on time, under strict observance of the stability criteria.
